FAQs and Average Rents in Vancouver, BC
How much is the average rent in Vancouver, BC?
As of July 2026, the average rent in Vancouver, BC is $2,686 per month.
How much is the average rent for a 1 bedroom in Vancouver, BC?
As of July 2026, the average rent for a 1 bedroom in Vancouver, BC is $2,377 per month.
How much is the average rent for a 2 bedroom in Vancouver, BC?
As of July 2026, the average rent for a 2 bedroom in Vancouver, BC is $3,255 per month.
How much is the average rent for a 3 bedroom in Vancouver, BC?
As of July 2026, the average rent for a 3 bedroom in Vancouver, BC is $3,928 per month.
Vancouver, BC

Renting Guide

Housing Market

A West Coast Gem Offering Stunning Landscapes And A Diverse Community.

Vancouver, nestled between the Pacific Ocean and the Coast Mountains, has long been a sought-after destination for those seeking a blend of natural beauty and urban convenience. Known for its stunning landscapes, the city offers a harmonious balance between outdoor recreational opportunities and vibrant city life. Established as a city in the late 19th century, Vancouver has grown into a bustling metropolis with a strong economy and a diverse population. Today, it continues to attract newcomers with its reputation for environmental sustainability and a high quality of life.

Despite its many attractions, Vancouver is also known for its competitive housing market. The demand for housing often exceeds supply, impacting rental prices significantly. However, for those who can navigate the market, the city offers a rich tapestry of cultural experiences, job opportunities, and a welcoming community.

Housing Market

Demand in Vancouver tends to outpace supply, so affordability is a real consideration. A couple of moves make a big difference: looking a little beyond the downtown core, and being open to shared housing. Local property managers can also surface options you won't always find on your own.

Typical housing type:

A wide range of apartment buildings and residential options.

Apartment Hunting

Vancouver's rental market is competitive, and finding affordable apartments can be a challenge. While budget-friendly options may be limited, especially in central areas, there are still a variety of 1-bedroom, 2-bedroom, and 3-bedroom rentals available across the city. From high-rise condos to charming houses, Vancouver offers diverse housing types to suit different lifestyles. Many properties feature desirable amenities, such as hardwood flooring and modern kitchens, though these can influence rental rates. Pet-friendly options are also available, accommodating those with furry companions.

Explore Property Types

Canada’s West Coast is a sunny, warm, mountain paradise. It seems like everyone wants to live there, so we are sure you will find the right type of property that fits your needs.

Apartments

Apartment hunting in Vancouver can be stressful as the city is famous for its high prices. But that's for good reason, Vancouver is one of the most desirable places to live in Canada. Check out Vancouver apartments for rent to find your taste of the west coast lifestyle.

Basements

In Vancouver, a lot of homeowners will offset the cost of ownership by converting their basement into an apartment. Vancouver basement apartments for rent can be a great option for rent, but make sure the conversion is fully legal. A surprising amount of conversions are done without proper permits.

Townhouses

Single family homes in Vancouver come at a hefty price tag. Vancouver townhouses for rent present a slightly more affordable option. Since you’ll be responsible for more of the property, ask the owner about maintenance responsibilities; a house falling apart will get annoying really fast.

Houses

Having your own single family home in Vancouver is honestly the ultimate flex. Alternatively, a lot of Vancouver houses for rent are laneway houses which are basically a really bougie garage that has been converted to a living space. They are way more affordable and require less work than regular homes.

Rooms

Unless you are prepared to spend big dollars for a place in Vancouver, sharing rent is a must. One of the best options for people looking to save a few bucks is to find rooms for rent in Vancouver. Be careful to find the roommates that are right for you. Anyone who has lived with a total slob before knows what we are talking about.

Condos

Most of the available residential properties in downtown Vancouver are condos. Vancouver condos for rent can get you deep in the heart of Canada’s most desirable city. They won’t come cheap though so make a plan to budget your expenses from the get go. Affording groceries and food is kind of a necessity too.

Look for the Amenities you want

Living a positive lifestyle in Vancouver is easy. If you are ready to pay a premium, the cities diverse offerings are ready to be your new home

Wheelchair Access

With all the new builds in the city, chances are you won’t have trouble finding options downtown. Vancouver wheelchair accessible apartments for rent are easy to find with elevators, ramps, and ground level apartments to suit your needs.

Pool

Sometimes you'll want to go for a swim but won’t feel like heading straight to the beach. Developers in Vancouver offer state of the art facilities for residents to enjoy. Vancouver apartments for rent with a pool are common and are a great way to meet your neighbours. Be friendly when going for a dip and you may just be invited to the next sushi night.

Gym

Beautiful weather means beautiful people. Health and fitness is important in Vancouver so take advantage of Vancouver apartments with a gym to get that year-round summer body.

Fireplace

The city rarely gets really cold so Vancouver apartments for rent with fireplaces will likely be more decorative than functional. Be careful if it is an electric fireplace as hydro is notoriously expensive in Vancouver.

Dishwasher

If you are not taking advantage of some of Vancouver's world class seafood, then why are you even living there? Vancouver apartments with a dishwasher help with the clean-up after a good feast. Don’t run it too often though, British Columbia suffers from water shortages that can affect price and availability.

Balcony

The Vancouver skyline is incredible – where else can you look at mountains then turn around and look at the ocean? Vancouver apartments for rent with a balcony are everywhere and definitely worth a potential upcharge.

Air Conditioning

You know the stereotype that Canadians live in igloos? These people have never been to Vancouver. The weather is warm here, so with Vancouver apartments with air conditioning you can expect to keep the air running a lot longer than normal. Be wary of hydro prices if it is a window or wall unit, but you can't really put a price on comfort anyways.

Washer and Dryer

Vancouver apartments with a washer and dryer are in no short supply. The high amount of new builds means that ensuite laundry can be found easily. But some buildings still have communal facilities. Ask the owner/manager about this when you tour.

Specialty Housing Filters

Housing in Vancouver is not as simple as just finding any old place and moving in. Rent is expensive so be sure to find the housing situation that fits your needs.

Pet Friendly

Vancouver has plenty of outdoor space to keep you and your pet happy. But if your little fur baby is a homebody check pet friendly rentals in Vancouver and ask the owner/property manager about their policy. A noisy dog in a high density building may not be the best fit.

Furnished

Vancouver draws a lot of people from overseas to the city. Coming from far away means you may struggle to bring furniture. Furnished apartments for rent in Vancouver solve that problem. Check with the owner about quality and what exactly they offer. Chances are you will still need to buy a few more things.

Short-Term

Moving to Vancouver for a temporary work term? Short term rentals in Vancouver can be found easily. Oftentimes it will be a sublet or lease transfer. So make sure to speak to potential roommates before signing anything. You want to make sure your lifestyles are compatible.

Corporate Housing

Vancouver is an economic hub, so you might find yourself relocating to the city for work. Vancouver corporate housing is communities and buildings with professional friendly environments. Ask about available amenities and furnishings as they are common.

Student Housing

The University of British Columbia is one of the world's finest schools. Situated right in the heart of the city, Student Housing in Vancouver is plentiful and in convenient locations. Tip – find a group of friends to live with. Sharing rent and utilities will make life way more affordable in Vancouver

Affordable Housing

We don’t know what to tell you here, cheap apartments for rent in Vancouver are not the easiest to find. There are some neighbourhoods with decent prices, but practice caution when searching. A really low price in Vancouver probably means a significant drop in quality.

Luxury Rentals

Vancouver is beautiful and so are the properties. Hardwood floors, new appliances, great views are commonplace. If you have the resources, why not enjoy Vancouver to its full potential. Check out luxury apartments in Vancouver for your taste of the high life.

Residents

Vancouver's residents are drawn to its natural beauty and active lifestyle, fostering a community that values health and wellness. The city is highly diverse, with a vibrant mix of cultures and languages, contributing to its rich cultural tapestry. Vancouverites are known for their progressive outlook and engagement with social issues, creating an inclusive atmosphere. Although the cost of living can be high, the city's appeal lies in its sense of community and the opportunities it offers for both personal and professional growth.

Neighbourhood

Vancouver's neighbourhoods each offer unique character and amenities, from the historic charm of Gastown to the bustling energy of Granville Street. Stanley Park, a cornerstone of the city, provides a green escape in the urban environment, while the Pacific Ocean and nearby mountains offer a breathtaking backdrop. The city boasts a variety of educational institutions, including UBC and Simon Fraser University, catering to a wide range of academic pursuits. With a comprehensive transit network, residents can easily access shopping, dining, and recreational activities throughout the region.

Landmarks:

Stanley Park

Granville Island

Vancouver Aquarium

Vancouver City Hall

Brockton Point Totem Pole

Waterfront Station

A-maze-ing Laughter

Library Square

Vancouver Lookout

Lions Gate Bridge

Gastown Steam Clock

Robson Street

Chinatown

Life & Style

Vancouver is celebrated for its commitment to work-life balance, emphasizing health, fitness, and leisure. Residents enjoy an abundance of outdoor activities, from strolling through Stanley Park to skiing on nearby slopes. The city's culinary scene is vibrant, with numerous dining options reflecting its multicultural community. Public transit, including buses and SkyTrain, connects neighbourhoods efficiently, making it easy to explore all that Vancouver has to offer. Whether enjoying the arts, engaging in sports, or simply relaxing with friends, Vancouver's lifestyle is both enriching and diverse.
